evidence.claim: The detector reads frames with a phase-(0,0) strided slice zarr[t, ::dz, ::dy, ::dx] at inference and in training, with no phase jitter. Peaks are decoded as coarse_index*ds with no +0.5*ds centring and cast to int16.

The detection target is a single positive voxel at floor(gt/ds) (.long()), trained with weighted BCE. The heatmap is therefore a posterior over the coarse floor cell, not a Gaussian. An ideal phase-d network predicts floor((y-d)/4), so argmaxes at 4 diagonal phases fix y to about 1 full-res pixel. DARK/Taylor decoding assumes a Gaussian heatmap, so fitting it to our logits is a guess.
evidence.source: train_unet_transformer.py l.541-593; DARK, Zhang et al. CVPR 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.06278

evidence.claim: Shift-and-stitch works as the hypothesis says: f^2 shifted inputs with the outputs interlaced, equivalent to filter rarefaction. FCN chose learned in-network upsampling over it, so it is a valid but secondary technique.
evidence.source: Long, Shelhamer, Darrell, FCN sec. 3.2, https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.4038 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/1605.06211

evidence.claim: Strided CNNs and U-Nets are not shift-equivariant. Outputs can change a lot under sub-stride input shifts, so the phase-shifted passes can carry phase-dependent bias and jitter, not just extra information.
evidence.source: Zhang 2019, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.11486; Chaman & Dokmanic CVPR 2021 (APS), https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/papers/Chaman_Truly_Shift-Invariant_Convolutional_Neural_Networks_CVPR_2021_paper.pdf; APS-U for U-Net, https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.04040

evidence.claim: Local dose-response contradicts the hypothesis's upper bound. On 24 videos (12 per embryo, raw ILP graph, per-frame Hungarian at 7 um) I added one more xy quantisation (uniform jitter of width 1.625 um, 5 seeds). It cost only -0.0021 (44b6) and -0.0013 (6bba) edge recall. Width 0.81 um cost -0.0003 / -0.0009. Because the loss is convex, perfectly removing the existing xy quantisation is worth at most about +0.001-0.002 edge recall before linefit, and less after.

Swap and u_diverted/v_taken FN have GT-to-match offsets of about 3.9-4.5 um. Grid noise is 0.47 um RMS per axis, so de-quantisation cannot move those matches by the several um needed. The +0.048 oracle is not reachable by this mechanism.

Measured GT-minus-pred offsets: mean (z,y,x) um 44b6 [0.20,0.24,-0.05], 6bba [0.90,0.33,0.17]; sd about 0.9-1.8 um per axis; 6bba median z offset +1 slice. The y bias of about +0.3 um matches the floor convention, partly cancelled by flip TTA (flipped views round the other way). Quantisation is about 20% of xy variance and about 10% of 3D variance, so full xy+z refinement cuts RMS by an estimated 6-8% before linefit.

Transfer counter-evidence: a heuristic sub-voxel peak refinement (Eric, rank 77) gave +0.0078 local and -0.002 on the LB twice. A constant offset correction (Le Quang Canh) lost 0.0031 on the LB. Only the learned x138 head transferred (+0.007).

Writer and replay both apply int(round()) to z,y,x. A polyphase xy refinement lands on the 0.406 um full-res grid and survives this rounding. A z refinement does not (z plane spacing 1.625 um) unless float output is adopted (sibling idea float-output-coords, +0.00165 local).

The public V1284 head's outputs are sub-um (q50 0.40 um shift). De-quantisation alone predicts about -11.7% median centre error (sqrt(1.72^2-0.81^2)=1.52), close to the head's -10.4%. Polyphase and the head therefore largely target the same error, and the overlap is probably large (guess).

implementation_notes:
WHERE: predict_unet_transformer.predict_video, after the phase-0 TTA peak extraction and before coords.astype(int16) (l.494-497). Keep the node set, probabilities, NMS and the phase-0 features used by the edge transformer unchanged. Only refine positions.

PHASES: use DIAGONAL shifts (d,d) with d in {1,2,3} on (y,x). These are 3 extra passes with the PRIMARY seed, no rot/flip TTA. That gives 4 distinct phases on each axis, where the proposed {(0,2),(2,0),(2,2)} gives only 2 per axis. Input: zarr[t_window, :, d::4, d::4]. Pad or crop to the model's 64x256x256 target shape. The zarr has 1024 px, so a d-offset slice has 255 or 256 rows; pad by edge replication so no trilinear interpolate is triggered. The WHOLE temporal window must use the same phase. Normalise with the same q_low/q_high.

PER-PEAK ESTIMATE (floor convention): for peak at full-res y0 and phase d, look in the phase logit map at rows j in {floor((y0-d)/4) + {-1,0,1}}, with the same z and a ±1 window in x. Take the argmax j_d and set yhat_d = 4*j_d + d. Final y = mean over d in {0,1,2,3} of yhat_d, + 1.5 px (the floor-cell centre). Do the same for x. Optionally use a 3-point parabola on the logits along each axis as a tie-breaker (guess; the target is not Gaussian).

GUARDS: (1) Phase consistency: if any yhat_d disagrees with the median by more than 4 px (1 coarse cell), or the phase peak logit is more than 2 below the phase-0 peak logit, keep the original coordinate. (2) Clip |shift| <= 1.2 um per axis. (3) PER-VIDEO RECENTRING: subtract the median (refined - original) shift per axis per video. This leaves pure de-quantisation and no global offset, because constant offsets lost 0.0031 on the LB. Also test an arm without recentring, since the +1.5 px term is a principled floor de-bias, but it is exactly the thing the Le Quang Canh evidence warns about. (4) z: stride is 1, so polyphase adds nothing. Skip z unless float output ships.

PITFALLS: CNNs are not shift-equivariant (Zhang 2019; APS 2021), so phase maps can be biased and the recentring plus consistency check are mandatory. The detector was trained on all 199 train videos. The phase-shifted pixels are unseen, but the nuclei are memorised, so the lab is still optimistic. Flip TTA already half de-biases the floor convention: flipped views round toward ceil. Refine against the TTA-averaged coordinate, not the raw primary argmax. Downstream gates (tight 5.5 um, gap 5.0 um, linefit 0.8) were tuned on grid coordinates. Keep them fixed in the first test. Cost is 3 extra primary passes against 16 today, about +19% GPU time.
refined_change: Label-free polyphase xy de-quantisation of the existing nodes. In predict_video, run the primary UNet on 3 diagonally phase-shifted strided inputs zarr[t, :, d::4, d::4], d = 1, 2, 3, with the same temporal window and normalisation and no rot/flip TTA. For each phase-0 TTA peak, take each phase's argmax within ±1 coarse cell and set yhat_d = 4*j_d + d (same for x). Refined coordinate = mean_d yhat_d + 1.5 px, with three guards: skip the peak if the phases disagree by more than 4 px, clip the shift at 1.2 um, and subtract the per-video median shift. Nodes, probabilities, NMS and edge-transformer features stay unchanged. Write xy at full-res integer voxels (survives the int(round()) writer). Leave z alone unless float output ships. Arms: (A) base; (B) polyphase with recentring; (C) polyphase without recentring (tests floor de-bias); (D) V1284 head coordinates; (E) mean of B and D. Do NOT chain the head after polyphase: the head was trained on grid-coordinate features and residuals.
refined_lab_test: GPU capture needed; the replay lab has no logits. One Kaggle T4 kernel, or friend A's 5070 Ti, primary seed only. Phase 1 (about 15 GPU-min): 24 videos (12 44b6 + 12 6bba, the same ones as the jitter study) x 100 frames x 3 phases. For every raw node in friend A's cache, keyed by (t,z,y,x), store the refined y,x and the consistency flag. Readout, no scorer: GT-to-matched-node distance (official 7 um matching) on raw ILP solution nodes. KILL if the median drop is under 5% on either embryo against grid coordinates, or if the recentring shift sd across videos is over 0.3 um (sign of a phase bias). The ideal-case ceiling is about -6 to -8% RMS before linefit. Phase 2, only if Phase 1 passes: capture all 199 videos (about 1.5 GPU-h), then run the Kaggle-CPU replay lab with refined xy substituted into the raw nodes, ILP topology and probabilities fixed, and all post-processing re-run. SELECTION (64 6bba), then one CONFIRMATION (135). Gate: >= +0.002 overall, >= +0.001 per embryo, >= 55% of videos gaining, 90% CI > 0, N_pred identical. Run arms B/C/E against A and D. Expect it to fail the +0.002 gate on top of the head (the dose-response bound is about +0.001-0.002 before linefit). Treat it as a stand-alone substitute or complement for the head only if the head port stalls.
expected_gain: Guess: +0.000..+0.001 public on top of the V1284 head, since both remove the same grid error. +0.001..+0.002 without the head. It is bounded by the measured dose-response (one extra xy quantisation costs only -0.001..-0.002 of edge recall before linefit). The hypothesis's +0.048 swap/diverted oracle is not reachable: those offsets are about 4.4 um against 0.47 um grid noise. Transfer risk is medium-high: heuristic sub-voxel refinement lost 0.002 on the LB twice for another team.
